name: Earl of Coventry
description: Earl of Coventry is a classic English 'Stops' or matching round game, closely related to Snip Snap Snorum. Unlike many complex card games, it is defined by its rhythmic verbal component - players recite rhyming phrases as they match the ranks played by their opponents. The game is a fast-paced shedding contest where the primary goal is to reach the 'stop' card (the fourth card of a rank) to regain control of the lead. Historically popular as a Victorian-era parlor game, it remains a charming social exercise in rhythm and rank tracking.

content.text: Earl of Coventry is a classic English 'Stops' or matching round game, closely related to Snip Snap Snorum. Unlike many complex card games, it is defined by its rhythmic verbal component - players recite rhyming phrases as they match the ranks played by their opponents. The game is a fast-paced shedding contest where the primary goal is to reach the 'stop' card (the fourth card of a rank) to regain control of the lead. Historically popular as a Victorian-era parlor game, it remains a charming social exercise in rhythm and rank tracking.

Originating in 18th-century England, it is part of a broad family of 'rhyming games' that were common before the rise of trick-taking dominance. The name refers to the Earl of Coventry, though whether it honors a specific historical figure or simply used the name for its phonetic fit in the rhyme is debated.
4 to 8 players; best with a larger group to ensure cards are widely distributed.
The entire deck is dealt out one by one. It does not matter if some players have one card more than others.
